sections.title: The Science of Making & Breaking Habits

items.q: What should you remember about **Habits ≠ reflexes**?
items.a: **Reflexes are hard-wired (blink,** withdraw from heat); habits are neuroplasticity-driven learned sequences.

items.q: What should you remember about **Limbic friction is measurable**?
items.a: **Too alert/anxious OR too** tired/unmotivated both block execution; match habit difficulty to phase neurochemistry.

items.q: What should you remember about **Linchpin habits must be enjoyable**?
items.a: **Only habits you like** can reliably pull harder habits along.

items.q: What should you remember about **Context dependence reveals depth**?
items.a: **Strong habits survive travel,** schedule shifts; weak ones collapse outside home routine.

items.q: What should you remember about **Scheduling time < anchoring state**?
items.a: **Rigid "10 AM every day" breaks** under context change; phase windows (0–8 h after wake) flex while preserving neurochemical support.

items.q: What should you remember about **Phase 1 for hard habits**?
items.a: **Leverage natural norepinephrine/dopamine/cortisol elevation +** sunlight/exercise/cold/caffeine/fasting to override friction on the behaviors you resist most.

items.q: What should you remember about **Phase 3 for consolidation**?
items.a: **Sleep-dependent neuroplasticity; low light, lower** body temp, NSDR/yoga nidra for habits that require calm (not high-friction work).

items.q: What should you remember about **Task-bracketing + dopamine spotlight**?
items.a: **Positively anticipate the whole sequence (shoes → door** → run → hunger → meal), not just the miserable middle; honest about difficulty, reward the envelope.

items.q: What should you remember about **21-day system trains meta-habit**?
items.a: **Missing 1–2 of 6 daily** targets is feature, not failure; tests automaticity days 22–28 without the list.

items.q: What should you remember about **Breaking habits**?
items.a: Long-term synaptic depression; insert **positive cargo** immediately after the unwanted behavior; avoid notification-based reminders.
